extracted_by: hand, T-0291 — the Democrat read, September 1834
note: Vol. I No. 43. The town is on page 3. Column 2 is the Tesseract fallback and carries the week's own matter — a marriage, a death, the marine list, Dr. Temple's store house and wharf, a dissolution and a caution — with a narrow strip of the neighbouring column's debris down its LEFT edge, which is quoted as it stands rather than cut, because it is letters and not text. Column 3 is the Vision reading of the standing advertisements and is interleaved.

THE BRIDE'S GIVEN NAME IS NOT SUPPLIED: the segmenter has broken it across lines 2817 and 2818 as 'Josers' and 'enpy', which will not reduce to one reading, so the person is minted with the illegibility inside the name — the same treatment the unnamed merchant gets at 1834-09-17 c001. 'Avovstvs Boxix' is read 'Augustus Bonin': this batch sets U as V throughout its small capitals, and the surname's middle is a recognition-class n/x confusion. 'J. Dea' + 'Caton' is J. Dean Caton, who signs a Lasalle county estray notice as clerk in this same issue's neighbourhood and is the town's justice.

claims.notes: THE MONTH'S FULLEST OBITUARY, and one of very few claims in the corpus that names a woman as its subject rather than as a relict: Sarah Hoit, of Stafford county New Hampshire, died in Chicago on 16 September 1834 in her forty-third year. It is extracted whole because the reconstruction's population is otherwise built almost entirely out of advertisers, who are almost entirely men. 'Sara / Hait' and 'Hoit' are the same name printed twice in three lines; the wife takes the husband's spelling and both are minted separately, as this project never coalesces two names without a rule. 'Cem.' → '—Com.' (communicated) is recognition-class.

claims.normalized: For Rent. A LARGE three story Store House, 40 by 60 feet, with a wharf attache[d], of 60 feet front. Also, a handsome small Dwelling House with two rooms. Also, a large and beautifully [f]inished Store, on South Water-st[reet], by JO[H]N T. TEMPLE. Chicago, Sept. 20, 1834. 43
claims.notes: THE MOST BUILDABLE CLAIM OF THE MONTH, and one of the few anywhere in the corpus that gives a building's DIMENSIONS: a three-storey store house forty by sixty feet with a wharf of sixty feet frontage attached, plus a two-room dwelling house and a large finished store, all on South Water Street, all to let by Dr. John T. Temple on 20 September 1834. Forty by sixty and three storeys is far above the town's ordinary frame, and the sixty-foot wharf front matches the river-lot frontage the plat gives South Water. NOTE WHAT IS NOT SAID: the notice does not say the three are one property or adjacent, only that one man lets all three, so no single footprint is asserted here — the dimensions belong to the store house and the wharf, and the dwelling and the store are separate offers. Dr. John T. Temple also advertises two new four-room dwelling houses on 1834-09-10 (c009 there), which makes him the month's largest documented landlord. He is NOT merged with Dr. P. Temple, who does the dentistry in that same notice.

claims.notes: RULING 3'S VETO, EXERCISED — a dissolution dated 22 September 1834. THE FIRM IS NOT NAMED: the notice gives only the partners' signatures, so there is no business record for the veto to attach to and no `contradicts` flag is set on anything. Stevens & Murray are not otherwise in the corpus, and this is recorded so that a later pass which finds their firm elsewhere can attach the veto then. That is the honest shape of it: the evidence of a closure exists and the thing it closes has not been identified. 'I, STEVENS' → 'L. STEVENS' from 'settled by L. Stevens' two lines above, which is the same signature spelled legibly.

claims.notes: KINZIE'S WAREHOUSE PLACED AGAINST THE FORT — the clearest reading of this address in the month, which is why the claim is made from this issue and not from the three other insertions that carry it more damaged (1834-09-03 page 1 column 1 line 53 'Wise House, opposite to Fort', page 3 column 6 line 3458 'the wast end of ha WasE Hocee, opposite'; 1834-09-17 page 1 column 1 line 58 'CAne Horse, oppoete to Fort Dearbern'). The fort is the one fixed structure on the plat, so 'opposite Fort Dearborn' is an anchor the model resolves directly. NO STREET is recorded because the advertisement gives none: it places the warehouse against the fort and stops. Kinzie's own new-goods advertisement adds 'the east end of his Ware House' as the door, which is a detail of the same building.

claims.notes: The second half of the militia election the month began with: the northern battalion voted at the Mansion House in Chicago on the third Saturday of September (1834-09-03 c010), and the southern battalion votes at Ingersoll's in Plainfield on 4 October. Extracted for the BOUNDARY, which is the sharpest statement in the month of where Chicago's hinterland was reckoned to end: south of the Oak Woods, south of a line to Laughton's, south and south west of the Dupage. 'Bravntex' → 'Bea[ub]ien' is the same signature the 09-03 order carries as 'Besunirs'; two ruined readings of one known name, and the name is the town's.

claims.notes: ONE IMPRESSION OF THE STANDING LAKE STREET LAND-AGENCY CARD. The Democrat sets this advertisement, word for word the same, in every issue from 1834-05-14 to 1834-10-01 — twenty consecutive weeks, eighteen of which set the line ‘purchased and Sold, or by commi[s]sion’ recognisably (T-1051). The card is identified by its copy and not by its display line: the same trade (‘House and Land Agent’), the same offer of building lots in the town and the School Section, the same houses to let, and the same office on Lake street opposite Dr. Temple's. The display line is lost — 3406 closes J. K. Botsford's notice immediately above — and the trade line itself is inside the transcription's uncertainty mark, '[uncertain: Nonse end Leel gent.]'. THE PROPRIETOR'S NAME IS NOT READ HERE and none is supplied into the quote: the record's ‘W. G. Blanchard’ stands on T-0408's reading of the two impressions whose columns are NOT Tesseract fallbacks (1834-07-16 line 5527, 1834-09-17 line 3292) and on identity.json's declared firm merge, not on this impression. The street did not survive the left margin ('• al. apposite Dr. Templés.'), so the anchor is read and the street left null; the card's last lines are set out of order, the address (3413) above 'Enguire at the Offce ne' (3414).
